title: Two letters that ask you to slow down.
subtitle: The first of the Ha Mim family of surahs

row.title: the garden
sub: Ibn Mas'ud: I take my time

then: This surah opens a group of seven that all begin with Ha Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} Ibn Mas'ud said that when he reached the Ha Mims it was like reaching a beautiful garden, {reward}so he took his time.{/reward}
now: You open the app on the bus with four stops to go. The habit is to race through and tick the day's reading off. {idea}Here the letters themselves say: slow down.{/idea} You do not need to understand them to stop and pay attention.
old: Letters I cannot explain are something to get past quickly.
new: A sign I cannot explain is a reason to stop and listen harder to what comes next.
try: Read the next few verses of this surah slowly, out loud, with no phone notifications on.

title: This Book comes from the One who misses nothing.
subtitle: Who sent it, and what that says about Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the Book is from the One {idea}who cannot be overtaken{/idea} and from whom nothing is hidden, {idea}not even an ant under many layers.{/idea} In Makkah, people argued about where the Quran came from. This verse states it plainly.
now: You read advice online and wonder who wrote it, what they know, what they want from you. Most voices know a little and miss a lot. {idea}This one knows everything about you, including what you hide.{/idea}
old: This is one more source of advice among many.
new: The One speaking here knows me better than I know myself, and nothing can stop His word.
try: Before reading today, say quietly: this is from the One who knows me. Then read one page.

title: Forgiving and severe, held together so you keep both.
subtitle: Hope and fear in one sentence
then: Ibn Kathir notes that mercy and punishment are often named together in the Quran {idea}so that people stay between hope and fear.{/idea} He forgives what is past and accepts repentance for what comes. {trap}The severity is for the one who persists and turns away.{/trap}
now: Some nights you feel too far gone to ask. Other days you feel so safe you stop trying. {reward}Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance{/reward} comes first, for the first mood. The warning is there for the second.
old: Either I am beyond forgiveness, or I do not need to worry at all.
new: The door is wide open, and that is exactly why I should not keep walking away from it.
try: Name one sin you have not asked forgiveness for. Ask, in your own words, today.

title: Their busy, wealthy lives are not proof they are right.
subtitle: Do not be fooled by how well others seem to do
then: In Makkah the deniers raised objection after objection, while their caravans and wealth kept growing. Ibn Kathir says their going about the land means {reward}their wealth and luxurious life.{/reward} {idea}Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: do not let that deceive you.{/idea}
now: You scroll past someone who mocks everything you hold sacred, and their life looks perfect. Holidays, a new car, a big following. {trap}A small voice says maybe they are the smart ones.{/trap} {idea}Comfort is not a proof.{/idea}
old: If they are doing so well, maybe they have it figured out.
new: How well someone is doing tells me nothing about whether they are right.
try: Next time you feel envy scrolling, close the app and thank Allah for one specific thing.

title: Every nation had its arguments against the truth.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ is shown he is not the first
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}consoles the Prophet ﷺ{/idea} here. The people of Nuh and those after them all did the same: {trap}they plotted against their messenger{/trap} and argued with falsehood to knock down a truth that was plain.
now: You know you are right about something good, but the family group chat keeps throwing new arguments at you. It wears you down. {idea}This pattern is older than you.{/idea} Clever objections do not make the truth less true.
old: If I cannot answer every objection, maybe I am the one who is wrong.
new: Truth has always faced clever arguments. Losing a debate does not make it false.
try: Stop replying to one argument that is only draining you. Make dua for the person instead.

title: The same word that came true before comes true again.
subtitle: Past outcomes as a warning for the present

row.title: that was then
sub: it does not apply to us

then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}just as the word of punishment came true for past nations,{/trap} it holds for those in Makkah who rejected the Prophet ﷺ and fought him. The stories before were not just history. {idea}They were a mirror.{/idea}
now: You read about people who ignored every warning and think, I would never. Then you notice the warning you keep snoozing like an alarm. {idea}The lesson is for you, not for them.{/idea}
old: Stories of past nations are about other people.
new: Allah's word does not change, so their story is a warning I can still use.
try: Think of one warning sign in your life you keep ignoring. Write down one step to act on it.

title: The angels around the Throne are praying for you.
subtitle: Who asks forgiveness for the believers
then: In Makkah the believers were few, mocked, and in danger. This verse tells them {reward}the angels closest to Allah{/reward} pray for them. Ibn Kathir explains their words: {idea}Your mercy covers their sins and Your knowledge covers all their deeds.{/idea}
now: You feel alone. The night shift, the hard week, nobody checking on you. {reward}Right now, beings near the Throne are asking forgiveness for those who believe and turn back.{/reward} You are spoken about, kindly, in a place you cannot see.
old: No one is thinking about me or praying for me.
new: If I believe and turn back, angels near the Throne are asking forgiveness for me.
try: Make dua for one friend by name, without telling them. Angels say amin for you too.

title: The angels ask that your family be with you.
subtitle: Paradise with parents, spouses and children who were righteous
then: Ibn Kathir explains the angels ask Allah {reward}to bring believers together with their righteous families{/reward} so they delight in each other. Sa'id bin Jubayr said a believer will ask where his father, son and brother are, and {reward}they will be raised to join him.{/reward}
now: Think of the family photo on your phone. Your mother, your spouse, your kids. Some of the happiness you hope for is simply being together. {idea}Your good deeds can be done for them too.{/idea}
old: Paradise is something I will reach alone.
new: The angels themselves ask that I be with my righteous family there.
try: Make dua tonight to be with your family in Paradise, naming each one.

title: Being shielded from your own bad deeds is the great win.
subtitle: The last line of the angels' prayer
then: The angels end their prayer asking that believers be {idea}protected from evil deeds, the actions and their consequences,{/idea} as Ibn Kathir explains. Whoever is protected that Day has been shown mercy. {reward}That is the great success.{/reward}
now: You track wins: a raise, a good grade, a new follower count. {idea}The angels define success differently.{/idea} Being kept from the harm of your own worst choices is the win they ask for on your behalf.
old: Success is what I can show off.
new: The biggest success is being saved from the cost of my own mistakes.
try: Ask Allah today to protect you from the consequences of one specific mistake.

title: Regret will come too late to change anything.
subtitle: Self-hatred on the Day, and an older displeasure
then: Ibn Kathir describes the regret of those who refused faith: {trap}they will hate themselves for what brought them there.{/trap} They are told that Allah's displeasure, when faith was offered in the world and they refused, {trap}was greater still.{/trap}
now: You know the feeling: the exam you did not study for, the call you did not return before someone died. Regret that arrives after the door shuts. {idea}This verse moves the moment of decision to today, while the invitation is still open.{/idea}
old: I can deal with my choices later.
new: The moment that counts is when the invitation reaches me, not when regret does.
try: Pick one good thing you keep postponing and do the first small part today.

title: Twice dead, twice alive, and now they ask for a way out.
subtitle: A confession that comes after the chance has passed
then: Ibn Mas'ud linked this to 2:28: {idea}you were dead, He gave you life, then death, then life again.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says on that Day they will confess and {trap}ask to be sent back to do better,{/trap} and will be told there is no way back.
now: The confession they make there is the one you can make here, for free, tonight on your prayer mat. {reward}Here it is accepted.{/reward} The same words, said in time, change everything.
old: Admitting my sins is humiliating, so I keep putting it off.
new: The confession they wish they had made is one I can make now, while it still helps.
try: Tonight, before sleep, admit one wrong to Allah plainly and ask Him to forgive it.

title: They bristled at Allah alone, and relaxed when partners were added.
subtitle: The reason given for no way back
then: Ibn Kathir explains this is why there is no return: {trap}when Allah alone was called on, they disbelieved; when partners were added, they believed.{/trap} If they went back, they would do the same, as 6:28 says. {idea}The judgement belongs to Allah, the Just.{/idea}
now: You notice it in yourself: easy to pray, but your real trust goes to the boss, the contact, the lucky charm, the backup plan. {idea}Is your heart at ease with Allah alone,{/idea} or only when something else is added?
old: I trust Allah, plus a few other things just in case.
new: My heart should rest on Allah alone, not only when something else is propping it up.
try: Notice one thing you lean on more than Allah. Ask Him directly for that need today.

title: Signs everywhere, but only those who turn back notice.
subtitle: Rain, provision, and who actually remembers
then: Ibn Kathir explains the provision from the sky is rain, which brings out crops and fruits {idea}with different colours, tastes and forms from one kind of water.{/idea} He shows His power in creation, {idea}but only those who turn to Him take the lesson.{/idea}
now: It rains and you complain about the traffic. Lunch is fruit you never really looked at. {idea}The signs are not missing. The attention is.{/idea} The verse puts the key in your own turning back.
old: If Allah showed me a clear sign, I would pay attention.
new: The signs are already around me. A turning heart is what lets me see them.
try: Next time it rains or you eat fruit, stop for ten seconds and say who sent it.

title: Call on Allah sincerely, even if others dislike it.
subtitle: Sincere worship when the room disapproves
then: The believers in Makkah were surrounded by people who {trap}raised objections and mocked their worship.{/trap} After showing who remembers, the verse gives the instruction: {idea}call on Allah, sincere to Him in religion,{/idea} even if those who reject dislike it.
now: You are at a work dinner when the time for prayer comes. Or your friends roll their eyes when you say you are fasting. {idea}The verse does not ask you to argue.{/idea} It asks you to stay sincere to Allah anyway.
old: I will be more open about my faith when it is easier.
new: Sincerity to Allah does not wait for other people's approval.
try: Do one act of worship today that you usually hide out of embarrassment, calmly.

title: Revelation comes down to warn of the Day everyone meets.
subtitle: The Day of Meeting, and why messengers are sent
then: Ibn Abbas said the Day of Meeting is {idea}one of the names of the Day of Resurrection,{/idea} the Day everyone finds out about their deeds, good and bad. Allah, exalted above His creation, {idea}sends revelation to warn of it.{/idea}
now: You have a big appointment in the calendar and you prepare for days: the interview, the hearing, the scan results. {idea}There is one meeting no one can reschedule.{/idea} The Quran in your hand exists to get you ready for it.
old: The Quran is mostly something to know about.
new: The Quran is a warning sent ahead so I am ready for a meeting I cannot miss.
try: Ask yourself one question tonight: if that meeting were tomorrow, what would I fix first?

title: Whose is the kingdom today? Allah's, the One.
subtitle: The Day nothing is hidden and every king falls silent
then: Ibn Kathir says on that Day people will {idea}appear in the open with nothing to shelter or cover them.{/idea} He mentions the hadith where Allah asks, {trap}where are the kings of the earth, the tyrants, the proud?{/trap} Then the answer: the kingdom is Allah's, the One.
now: You hide things well: the browser history, the side of you only your phone knows. And you fear people with power over you, the manager, the landlord. {idea}That Day, nothing is hidden and no one holds power but Allah.{/idea}
old: The people with power over me now are the ones I really answer to.
new: Every title ends. The only kingdom left standing is Allah's, and I answer to Him.
try: Next time you fear someone's power over you, say quietly: the kingdom is Allah's.

title: No injustice today, not even a speck.
subtitle: Every soul repaid for what it earned
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah does not do {idea}even a speck of dust's weight of injustice.{/idea} A good deed gets ten times, a bad deed only one. He quotes the hadith: {trap}whoever finds other than good, let him blame no one but himself.{/trap}
now: You have been wronged at work, credit stolen, your side never heard. It eats at you. {reward}On that Day, every unfair thing is settled.{/reward} And the same fairness looks at how you treated the junior colleague, the cashier, your sibling.
old: Life is unfair and nothing will ever set it right.
new: Every wrong will be weighed with perfect fairness, including the ones I did.
try: Right one small wrong you did to someone this week: an apology, a repayment, a credit given.

title: A Day so near that hearts rise to the throat.
subtitle: The Approaching Day, and no friend for the wrongdoer
then: Ibn Kathir says the Approaching Day is a name of the Day of Judgement, {idea}called so because it is close.{/idea} Qatadah said hearts will reach the throats from fear, {trap}neither coming out nor going back.{/trap} No one speaks without His permission.
now: You have felt a small version: the doctor about to read the result, your heart in your throat. You call the friend who always helps. {idea}That Day, the friend you rely on cannot reach you.{/idea} What helps is what you send ahead now.
old: The Day is so far off it does not affect my week.
new: Allah calls it the Approaching Day. It is nearer than my plans assume.
try: Do one good deed today that you would want to find waiting for you on that Day.

title: He knows the glance and the thought behind it.
subtitle: The betrayal of the eyes and what hearts hide

row.title: the hidden wish
sub: what I would do if I could

row.title: He knows
sub: so I feel shy before Him

then: Ibn Kathir says this is said so that people {idea}feel a proper shyness before Allah.{/idea} Ad-Dahhak said the betrayal of the eyes is a wink, or {trap}saying you saw something when you did not.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said Allah knows when a look intends betrayal.
now: The second look on the train. The reply that sounds kind but hides a dig. The thing you say you did not see. {idea}No one in the room catches it. He does.{/idea} Not to shame you, but so you can catch it yourself.
old: If no one sees it, it does not really count.
new: Allah sees the glance and the wish behind it, so I can be honest with myself too.
try: Next time your eyes drift where they should not, lower them once and say astaghfirullah.

title: Only Allah judges with truth. The rest decide nothing.
subtitle: The Hearing, the Seeing, against gods that cannot rule
then: Ibn Abbas explained that Allah {reward}rewards good with good and evil with evil.{/reward} The idols people called on {trap}own nothing and decide nothing.{/trap} Allah hears all that His creatures say and knows all about them.
now: The comments section has decided you are wrong. Your extended family has a verdict too. It feels final. {idea}None of those judgements are the one that counts.{/idea} The One who heard the whole story judges with truth.
old: What people decide about me is the final word.
new: Only Allah, who heard and saw everything, gives the verdict that lasts.
try: When a harsh judgement about you stings today, tell Allah your side in a short dua.

title: Stronger nations built more, and it did not save them.
subtitle: Travel and look at the ruins
then: Ibn Kathir says the past nations were {reward}stronger than Quraysh and left buildings and dwellings{/reward} the Makkans could not match. Yet they were seized for rejecting their messengers, and {trap}no one could protect them from Allah.{/trap}
now: You walk past an old ruin on holiday and take a photo. Someone once thought those walls would last forever. {idea}Your career, your house, your savings are walls too.{/idea} Good to build. Not enough to lean on.
old: If I build enough, I will be safe.
new: Stronger people built more and still had no protector except Allah.
try: Next time you pass an old building, ask: what am I building that lasts past me?

title: Clear proofs came, and they still said no.
subtitle: The reason behind the ruin
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gives the reason: their messengers came {idea}with clear proof and definitive evidence,{/idea} and {trap}despite all these signs they disbelieved.{/trap} It was not a lack of information. It was refusal.
now: You know your sleep is wrecked by the phone. You know that friendship is harming you. {trap}The evidence is in, and you keep asking for more.{/trap} Sometimes the problem is not knowing. It is not wanting to change.
old: I would change if I were just more sure.
new: Often I already know enough. What is missing is the will to act on it.
try: Pick one thing you already know you should change. Take the first step before tonight.

title: Musa was sent with signs and clear authority.
subtitle: The story that comforted the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: a promise
sub: the truth wins in the end

then: In Makkah, people were plotting against the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}consoles him and gives glad tidings of victory,{/reward} as happened to Musa. The surah introduction notes this story answers {trap}the plots to kill him.{/trap}
now: You are in a long hard season: a job where you are the only honest one, a family where you are the odd one out. {reward}Allah tells you stories of people who stood where you stand and came through.{/reward} Read them as letters to you.
old: My struggle is unique and no one has been here before.
new: Others stood exactly here with less, and Allah carried them through.
try: Read the story of Musa in this surah this week as if it were written for your situation.

title: The king, the adviser, the rich man: one answer.
subtitle: Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun call him a magician

row.title: attack the messenger
sub: a label instead of an answer

then: Ibn Kathir names them: Pharaoh the king, Haman his adviser, Qarun the richest trader. They called Musa {trap}a sorcerer and a liar.{/trap} He notes every messenger heard the same, as 51:52 says: magician or madman.
now: Someone says something true that you do not want to hear. It is easier to say: they are extreme, they are crazy, they are a hypocrite. {trap}A label ends the conversation without answering it.{/trap} Notice when you do that.
old: If I can dismiss the person, I can ignore the point.
new: Labelling the messenger is how power avoids the message. I can do better.
try: Next time someone says a hard truth to you, reply to the point, not the person.

title: When the truth arrived, they answered with cruelty.
subtitle: A second order against the Children of Israel, and its failure
then: Ibn Kathir says this was a second order against the sons of the Children of Israel, {trap}meant to humiliate the people{/trap} so they would see Musa as a bad omen. Yet {idea}the plots of the disbelievers were doomed to failure.{/idea}
now: When you cannot win an argument, it is tempting to hit back another way: freeze someone out, cut their hours, spread a story. {trap}Pressure in place of a reply.{/trap} The verse says where that road ends.
old: When I am losing, I can use pressure to win.
new: Pressure used against the truth always goes astray in the end.
try: If you are using silence or pressure on someone to win, stop today and talk to them honestly.

title: The tyrant claims he is protecting the people's religion.
subtitle: Pharaoh dresses his plan as public concern

row.title: let me kill Musa
sub: and let him call his Lord

then: Ibn Kathir calls let him call his Lord {trap}the utmost in offensive stubbornness.{/trap} Pharaoh said he feared Musa would change their religion and spread corruption, and Ibn Kathir remarks, {idea}as if Pharaoh would be concerned about corruption.{/idea}
now: You catch yourself saying I am only worried about you, when really you are worried about losing control. The office rule, the family decision. {trap}Self-interest wearing the clothes of concern.{/trap} Check the real motive.
old: I am only doing this for everyone's good.
new: Sometimes my concern for others is cover for protecting my own position.
try: Before your next firm decision for someone else, ask: who does this really protect?

title: Musa's answer to a death threat was to seek refuge.
subtitle: Refuge in the Lord of both of them

row.title: I seek refuge
sub: in my Lord and your Lord

then: Hearing he would be killed, Musa said: {idea}I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that when the Prophet ﷺ feared people, he would say: {reward}O Allah, we seek refuge in You from their evil.{/reward}
now: A threatening message, a bully at school, a manager who has it in for you. Your first reflex is panic or a furious reply. {idea}Musa's first move was a sentence to Allah.{/idea} You can borrow it.
old: When I am threatened, I have to handle it all myself.
new: My first move against a threat is to seek refuge in Allah, then act.
try: Learn the Prophet's ﷺ dua: O Allah, we seek refuge in You from their evil. Say it once today.

title: Would you kill a man for saying, My Lord is Allah?
subtitle: A hidden believer speaks up in Pharaoh's court
then: This believer from Pharaoh's family {idea}hid his faith until the day Pharaoh said, let me kill Musa.{/idea} Then he spoke. Ibn Kathir notes Abu Bakr used {reward}these same words{/reward} when he pushed away the man strangling the Prophet ﷺ at the Kabah.
now: Someone is being torn apart in the group chat, at the staff meeting, at the family dinner. You have stayed quiet for months. {idea}This man shows there is a moment to speak.{/idea} He used calm logic, not insults.
old: It is not my place to speak up for someone in trouble.
new: There comes a moment when a calm, fair word for someone is exactly my place.
try: Next time someone is unfairly attacked in front of you, say one calm, fair sentence for them.

title: You rule today, but who saves us if Allah's punishment comes?
subtitle: Power as a blessing to guard, and Pharaoh's empty reply

row.title: Pharaoh
sub: I show you what I see

then: Ibn Kathir explains the believer told them {reward}Allah blessed you with this kingdom, so guard it by giving thanks.{/reward} Soldiers would not ward off Allah's punishment. Pharaoh replied, I show you only what I see, and Ibn Kathir says {trap}he lied, for he knew Musa was truthful.{/trap}
now: You have a little power: team lead, eldest sibling, the one who controls the budget. {idea}It is a blessing, not a proof that you are right.{/idea} And when you say trust me, I know what is best, check that you are not just protecting yourself.
old: Being in charge means my view is the right one.
new: Any power I hold is a gift that can go, and I owe honesty to those under me.
try: Ask one person who depends on you: is there anything I decide that feels unfair to you?

title: I fear for you a day like the old nations saw.
subtitle: The believer warns out of care, not contempt
then: Ibn Kathir says this righteous man {idea}warned his people of the punishment of Allah in this world and the next.{/idea} He calls them {reward}O my people{/reward} and says I fear for you, not against you.
now: You want to warn your brother about the debt, your friend about the relationship. It can come out as I told you so. {idea}This man's words start with my people and I fear for you.{/idea} Tone decides whether the warning is heard.
old: Warning people means telling them how wrong they are.
new: A real warning starts from love: I fear for you.
try: If you need to warn someone, open with one sentence about why you care about them.

title: Nuh, Ad, Thamud: Allah wants no injustice for His servants.
subtitle: What happened before was justice, not cruelty
then: The believer names the nations who rejected their messengers. Ibn Kathir explains {idea}Allah destroyed them for their sins and rejection,{/idea} and {idea}He wants no injustice for His servants.{/idea} What happened was His just decree.
now: When something goes wrong, it is easy to say life is cruel or I am cursed. {idea}This verse asks a harder, kinder question:{/idea} what part did my own choices play, and what can I change?
old: Bad outcomes just happen to people; it is fate.
new: Allah wants no injustice for anyone. I can look honestly at my own part.
try: Think of one recent setback. Write one choice of yours that fed it and one you can change.

title: He fears for them the Day of Calling.
subtitle: From history to the Day of Resurrection
then: After warning of a disaster like the old nations, the believer says: {trap}I fear for you the Day of Calling.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains this is {idea}the Day of Resurrection.{/idea} His concern reaches beyond this world.
now: You worry about the rent, the boss, the test next week. Those worries are real. {idea}This man's care for his people went further:{/idea} not only how they would live, but where they would end.
old: Caring for people means helping their life here go well.
new: The deepest care also thinks about where the people I love will end up.
try: Make dua today for someone you love, for their akhirah as well as their dunya.

title: That Day you turn and run, and nothing protects you.
subtitle: No refuge from Allah, no guide but Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains people will run, but as 75:11 says, {trap}there is no refuge; to your Lord is the place of rest that Day.{/trap} And {idea}whomever Allah leaves astray has no guide but Him.{/idea}
now: Your habit when things get hard is to run: change the subject, open another app, move to another city. {idea}There is one place running does not work.{/idea} The way out is to turn toward Allah, not away.
old: When it gets too much, I can always get away.
new: There is no running from Allah, only running to Him, and He is the guide.
try: Next time you want to escape a hard feeling, pause and make a one-line dua first.

title: You doubted Yusuf while he lived and missed him once he died.
subtitle: A people who obeyed a prophet only in worldly matters
then: Ibn Kathir says Yusuf {idea}held high office in Egypt and called them to Allah with justice.{/idea} They obeyed him in government matters but {trap}not in worshipping Allah.{/trap} When he died they said Allah would send no messenger after him.
now: You take the parts of faith that help your life: the calm, the community, the good name. The parts that ask you to change, you leave. {trap}That was Egypt's way with Yusuf.{/trap} Notice which parts you skip.
old: I can take the practical parts of guidance and leave the rest.
new: Following only the convenient part of a message is a quiet way of doubting it.
try: Name one teaching you follow only when it suits you. Follow it once today when it does not.

title: Arguing against truth with no proof seals the heart.
subtitle: Dispute without authority, and what it does to a person
then: Ibn Kathir says those who {trap}dispute the proof without any evidence{/trap} are hateful to Allah and to the believers. Whoever is like this, Allah seals his heart so that {trap}he no longer acknowledges good or rejects evil.{/trap}
now: You argue online for the win, not for the truth. You say things you do not even believe to beat the other person. {trap}Do it long enough and you lose the ability to tell the difference.{/trap} The heart stops listening.
old: Arguing to win is just a game; it does not change me.
new: Arguing against what I know is true slowly closes my heart to truth.
try: In your next argument, say once: you have a point there. Mean it.

title: Build me a tower, said Pharaoh, to mock the Lord of Musa.
subtitle: A building project as a public stunt
then: Ibn Kathir describes {trap}the arrogant, hostile defiance of Pharaoh{/trap}: he ordered Haman to build a tall fortress of baked clay bricks, as 28:38 says. Sa'id bin Jubayr said the ways meant {idea}the gates of the heavens.{/idea}
now: Sometimes you make a big show of asking questions about faith, not to find answers, but to look clever in front of others. {trap}A tower built for an audience.{/trap} Sincere questions sound different.
old: Mocking a belief loudly is a way of testing it.
new: A question asked to mock is a tower built for the crowd, not a search for truth.
try: Write down one real question you have about faith, and ask it sincerely to someone who knows.

title: His evil deed was made to look good to him.
subtitle: How Pharaoh's plan ended in nothing but ruin

row.title: I think he is a liar
I would know if I were wrong

then: Ibn Kathir says Pharaoh built the tower {trap}to deceive his people and make them think he could prove Musa was lying.{/trap} His own evil was made to look good to him. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said his plot led to {trap}nothing but ruin.{/trap}
now: You have done something you knew was wrong and felt clever about it. The excuse sounded perfect at the time. {idea}That feeling is the warning.{/idea} When a bad deed starts looking fine, slow down.
old: If it feels right to me, it must be fine.
new: Evil can be made to look good to me, so feeling right is not enough.
try: Ask one honest friend about a decision you feel very sure of. Listen without defending.

title: Follow me, I will guide you to the right way.
subtitle: The believer reclaims the words Pharaoh misused

row.title: Pharaoh
sub: I guide you to right conduct

then: Ibn Kathir notes this is {idea}in contrast to the false claim of Pharaoh,{/idea} who said I guide you only to the path of right conduct. The believer uses the same words, but {reward}he points to Allah, not to himself.{/reward}
now: Everyone online says follow me, I will show you the way: to money, to fitness, to happiness. {idea}The words sound the same.{/idea} Ask where each voice is really leading you, and who benefits.
old: Anyone confident enough probably knows the way.
new: Two people can say the same words. The real question is where each one leads.
try: Unfollow one account today that leads you somewhere you do not want to go.

title: This life is a passing enjoyment. The next is home.
subtitle: Temporary use versus a settled home
then: His people {trap}preferred this world, and it kept them from believing in Musa.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says he told them this life is {idea}insignificant and fleeting,{/idea} while the Hereafter is the home with no departure.
now: You spend weeks choosing curtains for a flat you will leave in a year. Fine. But you would not pour your whole savings into it. {idea}This world is the rented flat.{/idea} Enjoy it, and build where you will stay.
old: This life is the main event.
new: This life is a short stay. The home I am building is the one after.
try: Spend ten minutes today on something only the next life will reward.

title: Evil earns its like. Good earns provision without count.
subtitle: Man or woman, the believer who does good
then: Ibn Kathir explains an evil deed is repaid with {trap}only one like it,{/trap} while for the righteous believer, man or woman, {reward}the reward cannot be counted.{/reward} Allah gives an immense reward without end.
now: You feel your good deeds are small: the dishes, the patient reply, the coin in the box. {reward}Allah's side of the scale is not measured like yours.{/reward} Man or woman, young or old, the door is the same.
old: My small good deeds hardly count.
new: Allah repays evil exactly, and repays good beyond counting.
try: Do one small good deed today without telling anyone, and trust it is counted.

title: I call you to safety while you call me to the Fire.
subtitle: Two invitations going in opposite directions
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer asks: why do I {reward}call you to salvation, the worship of Allah alone and belief in His Messenger,{/reward} while you call me to the Fire? He was alone in a hostile court, {idea}still inviting them.{/idea}
now: Your friends want you at the party that ends badly, or in the side deal at work. They are inviting you somewhere. {idea}You can invite them somewhere too.{/idea} Pressure works both ways.
old: When everyone around me pushes one way, I have to go along.
new: I can be the one inviting others toward what is safe, even when outnumbered.
try: Invite one friend to something good this week: a class, a walk to the masjid, a charity drive.

title: They offered gods without proof. He offered the Forgiving.
subtitle: Ignorance on one side, the Mighty Forgiver on the other
then: Ibn Kathir says they called him to partners {trap}on the basis of ignorance, with no proof.{/trap} He called them to the Almighty, the Forgiver, who {reward}with all His might still forgives the one who repents.{/reward}
now: You picture power as harsh: the strict boss, the cold system. You fear Allah the same way and stay away after a sin. {reward}The One with all power is the one who keeps forgiving.{/reward}
old: Someone that powerful would never forgive me again.
new: All might belongs to Allah, and He uses it to keep forgiving those who return.
try: After your next mistake, turn to Allah right away instead of waiting until you feel worthy.

title: What you call me to cannot answer anyone, here or there.
subtitle: False gods have no claim, and every return is to Allah

row.title: idols
sub: no power to help or harm

row.title: the One who answers
sub: in this world and the next

then: Ibn Abbas said the idols they called him to {trap}have no claim in this world or the Hereafter.{/trap} Qatadah said they have no power to benefit or harm, and As-Suddi said they {trap}do not respond to those who call on them.{/trap} {idea}Our return is to Allah.{/idea}
now: At 2am you pour your worries into a search bar, a horoscope app, a lottery ticket. {trap}None of them can answer you.{/trap} The One you return to is the One who hears you now.
old: Anything that might help is worth calling on.
new: Only Allah can answer a call, here and in the next life.
try: Tonight, before you check your phone for comfort, make one sincere dua.

title: You will remember what I said. I leave my affair to Allah.
subtitle: The believer finishes speaking and hands the rest over
then: Ibn Kathir explains the believer tells them they will come to know the truth of his advice and {trap}feel regret when regret is of no use.{/trap} Then he says, in effect: {idea}I put my trust in Allah and seek His help.{/idea}
now: You said the honest thing to your parent or your friend. They did not listen. You replay it, draft a longer text, lose sleep. {idea}At some point, your job is done.{/idea} Leave the rest with the One who sees.
old: If they did not accept it, I have to keep pushing.
new: I say the truth kindly once, then I hand the outcome to Allah.
try: Think of one conversation you keep replaying. Say: I leave my affair to Allah, and let it go.

title: Allah protected him from everything they plotted.
subtitle: The lone believer is saved, the court is not
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saved him {reward}in this world, along with Musa, and in the Hereafter.{/reward} Pharaoh's people, with all their power, {trap}were drowned in the sea.{/trap} The man who stood alone was the one who was safe.
now: You took the honest path at work and now you feel exposed. The others closed ranks. {reward}The verse does not promise easy days, but it shows who is really protected.{/reward} Numbers are not safety.
old: Standing alone for what is right leaves me unprotected.
new: The one who entrusts his affair to Allah is the one who is truly protected.
try: If you are standing alone for something right, ask Allah for protection by name today.

title: Exposed to the Fire morning and evening, before the Hour.
subtitle: What happens between death and the Day
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse is a major proof for what happens in the grave before the Hour. He narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said: {trap}seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave,{/trap} for it is real. {idea}Death is not a pause.{/idea}
now: You think of death as a long sleep until the Day, so it feels far away. {idea}The verse says what follows death starts right away.{/idea} That is a reason to live well now, and to ask Allah for refuge.
old: Nothing happens between death and the Day of Judgement.
new: What I do now meets me soon after death, so I live and pray with that in mind.
try: Ask Allah tonight, in your own words, to protect you from the punishment of the grave.

title: We followed you, said the weak. Can you take some of this?
subtitle: Followers turn to the leaders they obeyed
then: Ibn Kathir says the weak followers will say to their leaders: {trap}we obeyed you and heeded your call,{/trap} can you carry part of our burden? Pharaoh's people are among them. The followers thought obeying would shield them.
now: Everyone at work cut corners because the manager did. Your friends joined in the mocking because the loudest one started. {idea}I was just following{/idea} feels like a shield. It is not one.
old: If I only followed orders, the blame is on them.
new: Following someone into wrong is still my own choice, and I carry it.
try: Notice one thing you do only because a leader or crowd does it. Decide for yourself today.

title: The leaders reply: we are all in it together.
subtitle: Those who were followed cannot carry anyone
then: Ibn Kathir explains the leaders will say {trap}we will not bear any of your burden; our own is enough.{/trap} Allah has judged between His servants, {idea}sharing it out by what each deserves.{/idea}
now: The influencer who told you it was fine. The cousin who said everyone does it. {trap}When the consequences come, they are busy with their own.{/trap} Choose whom you follow by where they will be when it counts.
old: The people I follow will look after me if it goes wrong.
new: Those I follow cannot carry my burden. Each of us carries our own.
try: Think of one voice you follow without question. Ask: would I follow this alone?

title: Ask your Lord for just one lighter day.
subtitle: A plea to the keepers, from those who cannot ask Him
then: Ibn Kathir says they know Allah will not answer them, so they ask the keepers {trap}to pray for even one day's relief.{/trap} They no longer have what every person in this world has: {reward}the right to call on Allah directly.{/reward}
now: You have a direct line to Allah right now: no appointment, no middleman, no waiting room. You can raise your hands at a red light. {reward}They would give anything for that.{/reward} You have it free.
old: Dua is something I get to when I have time.
new: Calling on Allah directly is a gift I will not always have. I use it now.
try: Make one dua right now, before you close this card.

title: Did your messengers not come with clear proofs? Yes.
subtitle: The one-word answer that closes the case
then: Ibn Kathir explains the keepers ask: {idea}was proof not established through the messengers?{/idea} They answer yes. Then they are told to call on their own, for {trap}the call of the disbelievers is in vain.{/trap}
now: You have heard it all: the khutbah, the friend's reminder, the verse that stopped you once. {idea}You cannot say nobody told you.{/idea} That is not a threat. It is a chance, while answering still changes something.
old: I can always say I did not really know.
new: I have been told. The question is what I do with it today.
try: Pick one reminder you heard recently and act on it once today.

title: Allah will help His messengers and the believers, here and there.
subtitle: Victory in this life, and greater on the Day
then: As-Suddi said prophets and believers {trap}may be killed in this world, but their call will prevail.{/trap} Ibn Kathir recalls how Allah gave the Prophet ﷺ helpers in Madinah, then Makkah, {reward}until his call spread east and west.{/reward}
now: You are the only one in your family who prays, or the only one at work who will not lie on reports. It feels like losing. {reward}Allah's help may not look like a quick win.{/reward} Often it looks like the truth outlasting you.
old: If I am on the right side, I should win right away.
new: Allah's support is certain, but it may come as the truth lasting, not a quick win.
try: Keep one good habit going today even though no one has noticed it yet.

title: A Day when excuses stop working.
subtitle: No excuse accepted, and far from mercy
then: Ibn Kathir says on the Day the witnesses stand, {trap}no excuse or ransom will be accepted{/trap} from the wrongdoers. They will be {trap}cast far from the mercy of Allah.{/trap}
now: You are good at excuses: I was tired, they started it, I did not have time. They work on people, sometimes on yourself. {reward}Today, an honest sorry still works with Allah.{/reward} The excuse can be swapped for repentance.
old: I always have a good reason for what I did.
new: Excuses expire. Honest repentance works while I am still here.
try: Replace one excuse you used this week with a plain apology to the person, or to Allah.

title: Musa got guidance, and his people inherited the Book.
subtitle: Patience turned a persecuted people into heirs
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {reward}caused the Children of Israel to prevail in the end{/reward} and inherit the land and wealth of Pharaoh, {idea}because of their patience in obeying Allah and following Musa.{/idea}
now: You are in the hard middle part: the slow job search, the long recovery, the family that does not understand. {idea}The story says patience is not wasted time.{/idea} It is how people become heirs.
old: Waiting patiently means I am losing ground.
new: Patience in obeying Allah is how the oppressed became the ones who inherit.
try: In one frustrating wait today, say alhamdulillah instead of complaining.

title: Guidance and a reminder, for people who think.
subtitle: Who the Scripture actually helps
then: Ibn Kathir says the Tawrah they inherited was a guide and reminder for {idea}those of a sound and upright nature.{/idea} Inheriting a Book is one thing. {idea}Being guided by it takes a mind that is open.{/idea}
now: There is a Quran on your shelf, an app on your phone, a beautiful copy from your wedding. {idea}Owning it is not the same as being reminded by it.{/idea} It speaks to the one who stops to think.
old: Having the Book at home is enough.
new: The Book guides the one who reflects, not just the one who owns it.
try: Read one verse today and write one sentence about what it asks of you.

title: Be patient, seek forgiveness, praise Him morning and evening.
subtitle: Three things for the long wait
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}your word will prevail and Allah does not break His promises.{/reward} The command to seek forgiveness {idea}encourages the whole Ummah to seek forgiveness,{/idea} and to praise Allah at day's end and day's start.
now: You are waiting for the results, the job offer, the marriage, the healing. Waiting is mostly empty hours. {idea}The verse fills them:{/idea} a little forgiveness, a little praise, at sunrise and sunset.
old: Patience is just sitting through it.
new: Patience is active: I keep asking forgiveness and praising Him while I wait.
try: Say subhanAllahi wa bihamdihi a few times this evening and again tomorrow morning.

title: Behind their arguments is only pride they will never satisfy.
subtitle: What really drives arguing without proof
then: Ibn Kathir explains they are {trap}too proud to follow the truth and submit to the one who brought it,{/trap} and their attempts will fail. Then: seek refuge in Allah, {idea}from being like these people.{/idea}
now: You catch it in yourself: arguing with your spouse long after you know they are right, because giving in feels like losing. {trap}That is pride wearing logic as a coat.{/trap} The verse says: ask Allah to protect you from it.
old: When I keep arguing, it is because I am right.
new: Sometimes I keep arguing only because of pride, and I ask Allah to free me from it.
try: In your next disagreement, notice the moment pride takes over. Say: you are right.

title: The sky is bigger than you. Bringing you back is easy.
subtitle: An argument for the resurrection from scale

key.label: What they accepted, what they denied

then: Ibn Kathir notes many Arabs {idea}accepted that Allah created the heavens and earth{/idea} but denied the resurrection. {trap}They accepted the greater thing and denied the lesser.{/trap} The One who made the sky can easily remake a person.
now: You look up from a dark field and see thousands of stars, and you feel small. Then you doubt He can bring you back after death. {idea}The stars are the bigger job.{/idea} Most people never put the two thoughts side by side.
old: Rising again after death seems hard to believe.
new: The One who built the sky can rebuild me. That is the smaller task.
try: Look at the night sky for one minute tonight and think about this verse.

title: The blind and the seeing are not the same.
subtitle: Nor the one who does good and the one who does harm

key.label: Does it matter how I live

then: Ibn Kathir explains that a blind man who sees nothing {idea}is not the same as a man who sees as far as his eyes reach.{/idea} In the same way, {trap}the righteous and the corrupt are not equal.{/trap} Little do people remember this.
now: Sometimes it feels pointless. The cheat got promoted, the honest one got overlooked. {idea}It looks equal from here. It is not.{/idea} Doing good is not wasted just because nobody clapped.
old: Good or bad, everyone ends up the same.
new: Living rightly and living wrongly are as different as seeing and blindness.
try: Do one honest thing today that costs you a little and that no one will notice.

title: The Hour is coming. No doubt about it.
subtitle: Certain, even if most do not believe
then: After the proof from creation, the verse states it plainly: {idea}the Hour will come to pass.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says most people {trap}do not believe in it, and in fact doubt it altogether.{/trap}
now: Your friends never talk about the Hereafter. Nobody at work does. It starts to feel unreal because no one mentions it. {idea}Truth is not a vote.{/idea} Something can be certain while most people forget it.
old: If almost nobody around me believes it, maybe it is not real.
new: The Hour is certain whether or not the people around me think about it.
try: Bring up the Hereafter gently in one conversation this week, in a natural way.

title: Call on Me and I will answer you.
subtitle: Dua is worship, and pride is what stops it

row.title: bothering Him
sub: I should not ask so much

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah, {reward}by His grace, encourages His servants to call on Him and guarantees to respond.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}supplication is worship,{/idea} then recited this verse. Those too proud to call on Him are warned.
now: You hate asking people for things. Asking your parents for money, your boss for a day off, feels like begging. {reward}Allah is the opposite: He loves to be asked.{/reward} Sufyan Ath-Thawri called Him the One who loves most those who ask.
old: I should not keep asking Allah for small things.
new: Asking Allah is itself worship, and He has promised to answer.
try: Ask Allah today for one small, ordinary thing you would normally not bother Him with.

title: Night to rest, day to see. Most do not say thanks.
subtitle: The daily rhythm as a gift
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah reminds us that He gave the night {reward}to rest from our activities{/reward} and the day with its light {reward}for journeys and business.{/reward} Yet most people do not show gratitude for it.
now: You scroll past midnight, wake up tired, curse the alarm. Then rush into the daylight to work. {idea}The whole rhythm is a gift you never asked for.{/idea} Thanks can start with how you treat your sleep.
old: Night and day are just how things are.
new: Rest at night and light by day are gifts from Allah worth thanking Him for.
try: Tonight, put your phone away ten minutes earlier and thank Allah for sleep.

title: That is your Lord, Creator of all. So why turn away?
subtitle: Turning from the Creator to things that create nothing
then: Ibn Kathir explains the One who made night and day is {idea}Allah, the One, Creator of all things.{/idea} So how can you worship {trap}idols which create nothing, being themselves hand-made and carved?{/trap}
now: Your own creations can start to rule you: the business you built, the image you curated, the plan you made. {trap}You serve what you made.{/trap} The verse turns you back to the One who made you.
old: What I built is what keeps me going.
new: Things I made cannot sustain me. The One who made me can.
try: Name one thing you made that you serve too much. Give that time to Allah once today.

title: This is how people before were turned away too.
subtitle: Ignorance and desire as the road away from truth
then: Ibn Kathir says just as Quraysh were led astray, {trap}those before them worshipped others with no proof, on the basis of ignorance and desires.{/trap} They denied the signs of Allah.
now: When you drift from prayer, it is rarely because of a strong argument. It is the late nights, the new friends, a want you do not want to give up. {trap}Desire does the steering.{/trap} Notice it.
old: If I drift from faith, it is because I have good reasons.
new: Usually what pulls me away is desire, not evidence.
try: Notice one desire that keeps pulling you from a good habit. Make dua about it today.

title: He shaped you, and shaped you well.
subtitle: Home, roof, form and food, all from Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah made the earth {reward}stable and spread out to live on,{/reward} the sky a protecting roof, and {reward}created you in the best and most perfect form,{/reward} with good food and drink. He made the home, the people and the provision.
now: You stand at the mirror and list everything wrong with your face. The filters, the comparisons. {reward}He shaped you and made your shape good.{/reward} The verse ends: blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
old: My body is a list of flaws to fix.
new: Allah shaped me and made my form good. I can thank Him for it.
try: Next time you look in the mirror, thank Allah for one part of you before criticising anything.

title: He is the Ever-Living. Call on Him sincerely.
subtitle: The One who never dies deserves your call
then: Ibn Kathir says He is {idea}the Ever-Living, who was, is and shall be, the First and the Last.{/idea} He mentions that Ibn Az-Zubayr said after every prayer, {reward}we worship Him in all sincerity,{/reward} and that the Prophet ﷺ used to say this.
now: You lost someone you leaned on: a grandparent, a mentor, a friend. The phone number still sits in your contacts. {idea}Everyone you depend on will one day be gone, except Him.{/idea} He is the one who always picks up.
old: The people I rely on will always be there.
new: Only Allah is Ever-Living. My deepest reliance belongs with Him.
try: After your next prayer, say slowly: la ilaha illallah, with sincerity for Him alone.

title: Once clear proof came, I could not worship anything else.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ states his position plainly

row.title: submit
sub: to the Lord of the worlds

then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ is told to tell the idol worshippers that {trap}Allah forbids worshipping idols and false gods{/trap} besides Him. Then the next verses give the evidence: {idea}no one but Him deserves worship.{/idea}
now: You know what is true but keep a back door open: the old habit, the lucky charm, the it cannot hurt. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ shows the next step after knowing: commit.{/idea}
old: I can know the truth and still keep my options open.
new: Once the proof is clear, the honest step is to submit fully.
try: Close one back door today: an old habit or charm that competes with your trust in Allah.

title: Dust, a drop, a clot, a child, an adult, an elder.
subtitle: Every stage of your life is in His hand

row.title: I plan my life
sub: all the way to old age

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah alone takes you through each stage, {idea}by His command and decree.{/idea} Some die before birth, some in childhood or youth, {trap}before old age.{/trap} Ibn Jurayj said this is so you may remember the Resurrection.
now: You have a five-year plan, a pension calculator, a bucket list for retirement. Good. But you also know someone who never reached thirty. {idea}The term is His.{/idea} Live today as if it counts.
old: I will have plenty of time to get serious later.
new: Every stage is from Allah and the end is set by Him, so today matters.
try: Do one thing today you have been saving for when you are older and more serious.

title: He gives life and death. He says Be, and it is.
subtitle: Nothing resists what He decides

key.label: How hard is it for Him

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}is the only One who gives life and death.{/idea} When He decides a thing, He says Be, and it is. {idea}He cannot be opposed or resisted.{/idea}
now: The diagnosis, the visa that is stuck, the debt that will not shrink. It feels like a wall. {idea}For Allah, nothing is a wall.{/idea} What He wills needs only one word.
old: My problem is too big to be solved.
new: Nothing is hard for the One who says Be, and it is.
try: Ask Allah today for help with the problem you think is too big, plainly and with hope.

title: See how those who argue against His signs are turned away.
subtitle: A moment of wonder at minds diverted from truth
then: After all these signs of creation, Allah asks the Prophet ﷺ: do you not wonder at those who {trap}dispute the truth by means of falsehood,{/trap} as Ibn Kathir puts it, {trap}how their minds are diverted?{/trap}
now: It is easy to shake your head at people who argue against the obvious. Harder to see your own version: the hours you spend justifying a habit you know is wrong. {idea}Read this as a mirror first.{/idea}
old: Only other people argue against what is obvious.
new: I too can argue myself away from what I know is true.
try: Catch one moment today where you argue with a truth you already accept. Stop and drop it.

title: They denied the Book and the messengers. They will come to know.
subtitle: A short, stern warning
then: Ibn Kathir says they denied the Book and {idea}the guidance and clear proof{/idea} the messengers brought. They will come to know is {trap}a stern warning and clear threat{/trap} from the Lord, like woe that Day to the deniers.
now: Everyone finds out eventually whether the warning was true. The only choice is when. {reward}Finding out now, through the Book, is a mercy.{/reward} Finding out later is the warning.
old: I will see for myself when the time comes.
new: I can learn the truth now from the Book, instead of finding out too late.
try: Open the Quran today and read the next page with the intention to learn, not just finish.

title: Those who lived unbound will be bound.
subtitle: Collars and chains for those who denied the Book
then: These verses continue the warning to {trap}those who deny the Book and the messengers.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the chains are attached to the collars and {trap}the keepers of Hell will drag them along.{/trap} Those who refused every limit end up with no freedom at all.
now: You tell yourself no one can tell you what to do. No rules, no limits, just your choices. {idea}This verse shows where unchecked freedom can end.{/idea} The real freedom is choosing good today, while you still can.
old: Freedom means no one tells me what to do.
new: Real freedom is using my choices well, while they are still mine.
try: Choose one limit for yourself today for Allah's sake, and keep it gently.

title: From scalding water into the Fire.
subtitle: The end the deniers were warned about
then: Ibn Kathir links this verse to 55:43-44, where those who denied Hell {trap}go between it and fierce boiling water.{/trap} It is the outcome of a life spent arguing against the signs of Allah.
now: Hard verses like this are not there to crush you. They are there for the moment you are about to cross a line you know is wrong. {idea}Remembering the end can stop you at the edge.{/idea} And the door of repentance is still open.
old: Thinking about Hell only makes me anxious.
new: Remembering the end is a mercy that keeps me from walking toward it.
try: Make the short dua today: O Allah, protect me from the Fire. Say it with hope.

title: Where are the partners you used to worship?
subtitle: The question asked when help is needed most
then: Ibn Kathir explains it will be said to them: {trap}where are the idols you worshipped instead of Allah? Can they help you today?{/trap} The moment they most need help is the moment their gods are gone.
now: Imagine every thing you lean on in place of Allah being asked: where are you now? The savings, the status, the people you please. {idea}This question is coming for all of them.{/idea} Better to ask it yourself today.
old: The things I rely on will be there when I need them.
new: Anything I put beside Allah will be gone when I need it most.
try: Ask yourself today: what do I trust that will not be there on that Day?

title: They vanished. We never really called on anything.
subtitle: False gods disappear, and their worshippers deny them
then: Ibn Kathir explains they will say {trap}their gods have gone and can do nothing for them,{/trap} then deny ever having worshipped them, like 6:23. Their whole life's devotion turns out to have been {trap}to nothing.{/trap}
now: Think of something you once lived for: a crush, a rank in a game, a follower count. Years later you can hardly believe it mattered. {idea}Some things look empty only in hindsight.{/idea} Ask now what will look empty later.
old: What I live for now will always matter.
new: Some things I chase will look like nothing in the end. I can choose differently now.
try: Write down one thing you spend hours on. Ask honestly: will this matter on the Day?

title: Because you exulted on earth without right.
subtitle: The angels name the cause: arrogant joy and excess
then: Ibn Kathir says the angels will tell them their suffering is {trap}recompense for exulting in the earth without any right, and for their extravagance.{/trap} It was not happiness that was wrong, but {trap}arrogant joy that forgot Allah.{/trap}
now: You get the promotion and post about it like you made it happen alone. You laugh at the one who failed. {trap}That is joy without right.{/trap} The same joy, with alhamdulillah and humility, becomes gratitude.
old: My success is mine to show off.
new: Joy is good when it thanks Allah. Joy that boasts and looks down is the danger.
try: Next time something good happens, say alhamdulillah before you tell anyone.

title: A wretched home for the arrogant.
subtitle: Arrogance is named as the defining trait
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {trap}a terrible final destination for those who arrogantly ignored the signs of Allah{/trap} and refused His proof. The surah keeps returning to one root: {idea}pride that will not submit to truth.{/idea}
now: Pride does not always look loud. Sometimes it is quietly refusing to say sorry, or never asking for help, or never admitting you were wrong. {idea}Humility is the antidote,{/idea} and it starts small.
old: Arrogance is something only loud people have.
new: Quiet pride that refuses truth is the root this surah keeps warning about.
try: Admit one mistake to someone today, plainly, without excuses.

title: Be patient. Whether you see it or not, they return to Us.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ may not see every promise fulfilled
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah commands the Prophet ﷺ {idea}to patiently bear the rejection{/idea} of his people. He did see much of it: {reward}Makkah and the Arabian Peninsula during his lifetime.{/reward} But the verse says even if not, all return to Allah.
now: You raise your kids well, plant a tree, start a project for your community. You may not see how it turns out. {idea}You do not have to see the end to be sure of it.{/idea}
old: If I will not see the results, why bother?
new: Allah's promise is true whether I live to see it or not.
try: Do one good thing today whose results you will probably never see.

title: Many messengers, most of their stories untold.
subtitle: Signs only by Allah's permission
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}consoles the Prophet ﷺ{/reward}: many messengers came before, and those whose stories are not told are many more. {idea}None could bring a sign except by Allah's leave.{/idea} When His command comes, it is decided with truth.
now: You think of the good people in history and know a handful of names. Most did their work unseen. {idea}Being unknown to people is not the same as being unknown to Allah.{/idea}
old: If my good work is not known, it does not count.
new: Most of Allah's messengers are unnamed to us. He knows every one.
try: Do one good deed today that will never be posted, praised, or known.

title: Animals to ride and to eat, made for you.
subtitle: Livestock as a daily sign of His care
then: Ibn Kathir lists the blessing: camels are ridden, milked and carry burdens to distant lands; cattle give milk and plow; sheep give food and milk; {reward}their hair and wool make tents and clothing.{/reward} {idea}All made for people by Allah.{/idea}
now: Your dinner came in plastic from a shelf. The milk in your tea, the wool in your jumper, the leather of your shoes. {idea}Every one of them traces back to animals Allah made for you.{/idea}
old: Food and clothing are just things I buy.
new: The animals that feed and clothe me are a gift Allah made for me.
try: At your next meal, say bismillah slowly and think of where the food came from.

title: On animals and ships you reach what your heart wants.
subtitle: Travel and getting to your goals as a blessing
then: The verse continues the list of what livestock give: {reward}many other benefits,{/reward} and the means to {reward}reach a need in your heart,{/reward} with ships alongside them. Ibn Kathir notes camels carried heavy loads on journeys to distant lands.
now: You board the bus, the plane, the ferry to visit family or reach a new job. {idea}You are carried.{/idea} The verse invites you to notice that every journey toward something you want is a gift.
old: Getting where I need to go is just logistics.
new: Every journey that brings me to what I want is Allah carrying me.
try: On your next trip, say the travel dua or simply thank Allah as you set off.

title: He shows you His signs. Which one will you deny?
subtitle: Signs on the horizons and in yourselves
then: Ibn Kathir explains He shows you {idea}His proof and evidence, on the horizons and in yourselves.{/idea} You cannot deny any of them {trap}unless you are stubborn and arrogant.{/trap}
now: Your heartbeat, the way a wound closes, your child's first word, the sunrise from the window. {idea}Signs are not rare. They are constant.{/idea} The question is which one you will keep walking past.
old: Signs of Allah are rare and hard to find.
new: His signs are everywhere, including in me. Ignoring them takes effort.
try: Find one sign of Allah in your own body today and thank Him for it.

title: More people, more power, more building. None of it helped.
subtitle: The surah returns to the ruins of past nations

row.title: only what I did for Him

then: As the surah closes, it echoes verse 21. Ibn Kathir says these nations had {reward}great strength, left traces in the earth and amassed great wealth.{/reward} {trap}None of that could prevent the punishment of Allah at all.{/trap}
now: You work overtime to build a bigger safety net: more income, more contacts, more property. Fine, but quietly you think it makes you safe. {idea}Earnings help here. They do not protect you from Allah.{/idea}
old: Earning more will make me safe.
new: What I earn cannot save me. Only how I lived before Allah can.
try: Give a small charity today from your earnings, as a sign of where your trust is.

title: They were pleased with their own knowledge and mocked the rest.
subtitle: Knowledge as a reason to refuse guidance
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}were content with the knowledge they had{/trap} and said they did not need what the messengers brought. Mujahid said they claimed, {trap}we know better than them; we will not be resurrected.{/trap}
now: You have a degree, you read a lot, you can win any debate at dinner. It is easy to feel you have outgrown faith. {idea}Knowing a lot about the world can make you deaf to what is beyond it.{/idea}
old: I know enough not to need guidance.
new: Worldly knowledge is good, but it can make me too proud to hear the truth.
try: Ask a question today about faith that you assumed you already knew the answer to.

title: When they saw the punishment, they finally said: Allah alone.
subtitle: Belief that arrives only when it is forced
then: Ibn Kathir says they affirmed Allah is One and rejected their false gods, {trap}but at the time when excuses were of no use.{/trap} He compares it to {trap}Pharaoh saying I believe as he was drowning{/trap} (10:90).
now: Everyone believes in the alarm once the smoke is in the room. {reward}The value of faith is believing before you see.{/reward} The words they said too late are words you can say today, and they count.
old: I will commit fully when I see proof with my own eyes.
new: Faith counts because it comes before seeing. Today the same words still count.
try: Say la ilaha illallah slowly today, knowing it counts because you have not seen.

title: Faith after seeing the punishment does not help.
subtitle: The way of Allah, and the open door before it

key.label: How long the door is open

then: Ibn Kathir explains this is {idea}the way of Allah with all who repent only when they see the punishment.{/idea} He cites the hadith: {reward}Allah accepts the repentance of His servant as long as the death rattle has not reached his throat.{/reward} With this, the surah ends.
now: The surah opened with the Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance. It closes by showing the door does not stay open forever. {reward}Right now, reading this, it is open.{/reward}
old: I can always repent later, at the end.
new: The door of repentance is wide open now, and I do not know when it closes.
try: Before you sleep tonight, repent sincerely for one thing. Do not wait for later.
